title: Coral and the Machine
premise: Yara Montrose smuggles forbidden memories through orbital customs aboard the Coral, a rusting freighter she inherited from her mother, who died carrying secrets about the colony world Vesperine. When a distress signal arrives in Vesperine's extinct native language — a language Yara's mother taught her in secret — Yara discovers the colony's 'forgotten' death was a deliberate purge, and the signal's sender holds the recording that proves it. Pursued by customs fleets and the warlord who ordered the purge, Yara must choose between selling the message to save herself or broadcasting it and igniting a war of vengeance. In the end she delivers it not to the warlords but to the survivors' hidden descendants, ending the war by making the truth impossible to bury — at the cost of the Coral, and nearly her own life.
about_author: Juniper Voss is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade transcribing dying oral histories along the Pacific coast. Coral and the Machine is their second novel, following the acclaimed The Salt Archive.

chapters.title: Contraband Heartbeats
chapters.summary: Yara runs a memory-shard shipment past Vesper Gate customs, hiding contraband inside recordings of her own childhood. POV: Yara. Establishes her loneliness, her debt to the fence Ovid Rell, and the Coral as her only inheritance. Emotional beat: guarded competence masking grief.

chapters.title: The Language Nobody Speaks
chapters.summary: Docked at Meridian Station, Yara receives a fragmented distress signal in Vesperine — the extinct language only her dead mother taught her. She translates enough to learn a name: Kel Adisa, supposedly dead twenty years. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the past knocking, unwelcome and undeniable.

chapters.title: Ovid's Offer
chapters.summary: Ovid Rell reveals a buyer — the warlord Sef Corrane's intelligence bureau — will pay a fortune for anything from Vesperine's final days. Yara refuses, but Ovid sells her location anyway. POV: Yara, with a cold flashback to her mother's last transmission. Emotional beat: betrayal dressed as business.

chapters.title: Running the Gate
chapters.summary: Customs cruisers lock down Meridian. Yara burns a forged manifest and threads the Coral through a debris field, taking hull damage to escape. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: exhilarating terror; the ship and pilot saving each other.

chapters.title: Kel Adisa, Alive
chapters.summary: Yara traces the signal to a derelict relay and finds Kel Adisa — a Vesperine archivist who faked his death, carrying the colony's final memory archive. He is dying of radiation sickness. POV: Kel. Emotional beat: a man who outlived his world by refusing to stop recording.

chapters.title: What the Archive Holds
chapters.summary: Kel shows Yara the archive's core: proof Corrane's fleet deliberately poisoned Vesperine's atmosphere and erased the record. The message must reach the Assembly before Corrane's amnesty vote. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Two Centuries of Silence
chapters.summary: Kel explains why Vesperine was purged: the colonists sheltered the descendants of a conquered people whose language carried land-claim law. Yara realizes her mother was Vesperine-born. POV: Kel, with Yara interludes. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed — she was always part of this.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: Corrane's hunter-ship Wraith finds them. Kel insists on splitting up: he'll draw them while Yara carries a decoy shard. POV: Kel. Emotional beat: quiet sacrifice from a man who has already died once.

chapters.title: Decoy
chapters.summary: The Wraith takes Kel's bait. Yara watches the relay burn on sensors, unable to confirm his fate. She grieves in the only way she knows: recording a memory of him. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief as cargo she cannot jettison.

chapters.title: Assembly Station
chapters.summary: Yara reaches Assembly Station and contacts Delegate Imara Senn, a reformist. Senn is sympathetic but warns the amnesty vote is in six days and Corrane's bloc controls the evidence committees. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: hope meeting machinery.

chapters.title: The Committee Room
chapters.summary: Senn submits the archive; Corrane's agents declare it forged and seize it. Yara is detained as an unlicensed courier. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the law itself as a weapon; institutional despair.

chapters.title: Cell 9
chapters.summary: In detention, Yara meets Toma Rell — Ovid's estranged daughter, an Assembly clerk who suspects her father's network. Toma offers to help if Yara can prove the archive is genuine. POV: Toma. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, family debts on both sides.

chapters.title: The Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Yara realizes the archive's authentication key is her mother's voice — her mother was the archive's original courier, and the key phrase is a lullaby only Yara knows. POV: Yara, flashback-heavy. Emotional beat: her inheritance was never the ship; it was this.

chapters.title: Breakout
chapters.summary: Toma springs Yara during a station power fault; they recover the seized archive from the evidence vault. The Wraith docks at Assembly Station — Kel, captured alive, is Corrane's proof-of-torture exhibit. POV: Toma. Emotional beat: fear converted to fury.

chapters.title: Corrane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corrane offers Yara her freedom and a fortune to surrender the archive, revealing he knew her mother — and that her mother once made the same offer to him, and died for refusing. POV: Corrane. Emotional beat: the villain as mirror; the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: What Survival Is Worth
chapters.summary: Yara, tempted, nearly takes the deal — until she finds Kel in a holding cell, still whispering Vesperine to keep the language alive. She chooses. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the thematic crux; belonging over safety.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Yara and Toma seize the Assembly's public broadcast array during the amnesty vote. Yara authenticates the archive with her mother's lullaby and plays Vesperine's final hours to every screen in the system. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: climax — grief made public, undeniable, incendiary.

chapters.title: The Vote That Didn't Matter
chapters.summary: The amnesty collapses; Corrane's fleet moves to seize the station. Kel, freed in the chaos, broadcasts the counter-order in Vesperine — and hidden Vesperine descendants across the colonies answer, revealing a resistance network Corrane never knew existed. POV: Kel. Emotional beat: the forgotten finding each other.

chapters.title: Coral Burning
chapters.summary: To cover the descendants' evacuation, Yara flies the Coral as a decoy against the Wraith. The old ship takes fatal damage; Yara ejects into the debris her mother once taught her to navigate. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: letting go of the last physical piece of inheritance.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Recorded
chapters.summary: Corrane is arrested by his own officers after his fleet defects. Yara, injured and shipless, records Kel's testimony — the first entry in a new, living archive. POV: Toma. Emotional beat: exhaustion, vindication, and the strange quiet after war is unmade.

chapters.title: The Lullaby in the Dark
chapters.summary: Weeks later, aboard a Vesperine descendant vessel, Yara teaches a child the language her mother taught her — completing the circuit of inheritance. She is offered a home and, for the first time, doesn't run. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Coral and the Machine
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Yara pilots a new ship, the Coral's name plate welded above the console, carrying open archives instead of contraband. A final transmission from her mother's old relay plays the lullaby — the machine remembering what the coral grew over. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: peace earned; memory as home.
